data.title: REAGENT WEIGHT LOG ⚗️
data.statement:
PAT logs every reagent Paul scavenges for his water filter. Each is written as a chemical formula: element symbols packed together with <<no spaces>>, each optionally followed by a count (a missing count means 1).

A symbol is <<one uppercase>> letter, optionally followed by <<one lowercase>> letter (H, O, Na, Cl, Fe, Cu…). The molar mass of a formula is the <<sum>> of each element's atomic mass times its count.

Atomic masses: {{H}}={{1}} · {{C}}={{12}} · {{N}}={{14}} · {{O}}={{16}} · {{Na}}={{23}} · {{Cl}}={{35}} · {{Fe}}={{56}} · {{Cu}}={{64}}

Output the <<total molar mass>> of the formula.
data.constraints:
1 ≤ length of [[S]] ≤ 99
[[S]] contains only the element symbols listed above, optionally each followed by a count 1–99.
data.inputDescription: Line 1: A string [[S]], a chemical formula with no spaces.
data.outputDescription: Line 1: An integer, the molar mass of [[S]].

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

PAT logs every reagent Paul scavenges for his water filter. Each is written as a chemical formula: element symbols packed together with no spaces, each optionally followed by a count (a missing count means 1).

A symbol is one uppercase letter, optionally followed by one lowercase letter (H, O, Na, Cl, Fe, Cu…). The molar mass of a formula is the sum of each element's atomic mass times its count.

Atomic masses: H=1 · C=12 · N=14 · O=16 · Na=23 · Cl=35 · Fe=56 · Cu=64

Output the total molar mass of the formula.
Input
Line 1: A string S, a chemical formula with no spaces.
Output
Line 1: An integer, the molar mass of S.
Constraints
1 ≤ length of S ≤ 99
S contains only the element symbols listed above, optionally each followed by a count 1–99.
Example
Input
H2O
Output
18
